inputs.concise_input_summary: Support across five Iran War Powers removal resolutions.
Support across two Lebanon War Powers removal resolutions.
Support across two Venezuela War Powers removal resolutions.
One excluded choice supporting repeal of the 1991 and 2002 AUMFs.

material_limitations: The country targets, resolution wording, dates, and House sessions differ.
The proposition is confined to the accepted Iran, Lebanon, and Venezuela War Powers patterns.
The AUMF repeal choice is a singleton and remains excluded at the Behavioral Semantic IR layer.
The record does not establish a position on all military intervention or every authorization question.
candidate_definitions.proposition: Across the accepted Iran, Lebanon, and Venezuela patterns, Foushee repeatedly supported War Powers measures directing the removal of United States armed forces from the bounded hostilities described in those measures.

relationship_basis.semantic_relationship: Three independently accepted repeated patterns use the same War Powers removal mechanism across three distinct country targets and share the same accepted direction.

candidate_definitions.relationship_rationale: The synthesis relates three already accepted recurring patterns by a shared legal mechanism and direction while preserving their distinct country targets. The AUMF repeal singleton is contextual only.
candidate_definitions.unresolved_ambiguity: Human review must decide whether the shared War Powers mechanism adds enough explanatory structure beyond the three accepted patterns.
candidate_definitions.why_synthesis_not_topic_grouping: It identifies a repeated cross-target relationship among accepted patterns that all concern directing termination of specified armed-forces involvement under congressional authorization mechanisms; it does not group every military or foreign-policy proposition.

candidate_definitions.competing_interpretation: Keep every country-specific proposition independent because the record may support only separate bounded choices rather than a cross-country boundary.

inputs.concise_input_summary: Mixed choices across four Ukraine-assistance measures.
One excluded choice opposing removal of Taiwan security-cooperation funding.
One excluded choice supporting a specific $3.3 billion Israel FMF reduction.

material_limitations: The countries, accounts, measures, and restriction mechanisms differ.
The Ukraine proposition is itself mixed and includes one whole-measure authorization.
The Taiwan and Israel inputs are singleton notable choices and remain excluded at the Behavioral Semantic IR layer.
No reason for the country-specific differences is inferred.
candidate_definitions.proposition: The accepted security-assistance record is differentiated rather than uniform: the Ukraine pattern is mixed, the Jordan pattern opposes assistance restrictions, an excluded Taiwan choice opposed striking security-cooperation funding, and an excluded Israel choice supported a specific Foreign Military Financing reduction.

relationship_basis.semantic_relationship: Accepted country-specific assistance propositions carry mixed or contrasting effects that bound any single-direction assistance conclusion.

candidate_definitions.relationship_rationale: The candidate explains why the accepted country-specific assistance inputs cannot safely compile to a general pro-aid or anti-aid conclusion. The excluded Taiwan and Israel choices remain contextual and contrast evidence rather than recurring patterns.
candidate_definitions.unresolved_ambiguity: Human review must decide whether the contrast is explanatory enough to retain as synthesis or should remain a dossier-only caution.
candidate_definitions.why_synthesis_not_topic_grouping: The relationship is an explicit interpretive boundary created by different accepted directions across comparable assistance choices, not a claim that every foreign-assistance proposition shares one position.
